Formulation  
Peter presents with depressive symptoms characterized by low mood, decreased appetite and energy, and anxiety symptoms of situational palpitations and breathlessness likely precipitated or exacerbated by stress related to work changes and possible untreated hypothyroidism after discontinuation of thyroxine. Physical symptoms warrant investigation to rule out medical causes, including blood tests for thyroid function and general laboratory screening. Protective factors include social support and engagement with care. Early medical and mental health intervention aims to address mood symptoms, physical health, and anxiety symptoms.

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Depressive symptoms with anxiety features  
- Patient Goal(s): Improve mood, increase energy and appetite, reduce anxiety symptoms  
- Clinical Goal(s): Complete blood tests including thyroid function; assess and optimize medical treatment; monitor mental health symptoms  
- Actions (Patient): Contact support via provided app number for blood tests; report any worsening symptoms or new concerns, including chest pain or changes in bowel habits  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Arrange blood tests (routine bloods including thyroid, anemia, liver, kidney, and vitamin levels); review results and arrange further physical examination if required; provide ongoing monitoring and mental health support  

Secondary Problem: Untreated hypothyroidism  
- Patient Goal(s): Reestablish appropriate thyroid medication management  
- Clinical Goal(s): Confirm thyroid status via blood tests; restart thyroxine if indicated; coordinate thyroid management with GP or specialist  
- Actions (Patient): Attend for blood testing; discuss medication adherence with clinician  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Follow-up blood test results; consider restarting thyroxine and liaise with endocrinology if necessary  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes; education included importance of blood tests, warning signs requiring urgent care (chest pain, changes in bowel habits, severe symptoms)  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Worsening low mood, increased anxiety, onset of chest pain, changes in bowel habits, vomiting  
- Coping Strategies: Not recorded

- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded
